accepted.evidence: Turner5754 gives Darrai and Wegal tatī father in the tāta family, alongside tat/tata father forms elsewhere. The source Darrai tātā belongs to this kinship-address family; retain its final ā rather than copying the comparator’s ī. The historical entry includes affectionate address to both younger and older relatives, not only the modern father sense. Source dar lect and unmarked/marked lengths preserved; the source supplies no page locator.

This is the dādda kinship family, retaining the exact Darrai sense and dialect rather than importing another dialect’s relationship label. Source dar lect and unmarked/marked lengths preserved; the source supplies no page locator.

Turner997 explicitly gives Pashai āī mother. Both Lehr ay and ai mother records fit that existing family and are retained separately.
